newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crude liftings seen slightly lower in Ma.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crude liftings seen slightly lower in Ma.

text.p: May loading schedules for the eight main British and Norwegian oilfield systems project fractionally lower liftings than in April, programmes released this week by operating companies show.

May liftings from Norway's Ekofisk, Gullfaks, Oseberg, Statfjord and Troll and Britain's Brent, Flotta and Forties systems are scheduled at 4.65 million barrels a day (bpd) down just 40,000 bpd from 4.69 million in April, the programmes show.
May programmes project 235 cargoes versus 230 in the shorter 30 days of April with two more each in May of Oseberg and Statfjord and Brent and one more of Ekofisk.

Flotta is scheduled to lift two cargoes less in May and Forties loadings are also slightly lower. Following are details of the May North Sea crude loading schedules, in standard-sized cargoes, with previous month comparisons:
* April Brent 39 cargoes plus 1.4 million barrels in topups, revised up two cargoes from original programme.
* May Brent 37 cargoes plus 1.43 million barrels in topups.
* April Forties was revised down by six cargoes or 3.3 million barrels.

Brent and Oseberg are shown measured in 500,000-barrel cargoes. Statfjord and Gullfaks are 855,000 barrels while Ekofisk are mainly 500,000 barrels. Forties cargoes normally vary between 400,000 to one million barrels. Flotta cargoes are normally 500,000, 600,000 and 650,000 barrels and Troll is normally between 400,000 and one million barrels.
